[Graph.c] Avoid cleaning garbage values in graph_remove_vertex

Instead of clearing the edges and weights arrays when removing an
element, leave them as garbage, and only clear them when a new
vertex is added. This way, we avoid the effort of clearing the
arrays until they are needed again.

Let's say we remove 1000 vertices from the graph. We don't need to
iterate through the whole edges and weights arrays 1000 times (O n)
Instead, forget about them, and as we start to add new vertices,
populate the arrays with the default values.

LinkedList: Fix bug in remove_front and remove_back functions

When there was only one element in the list (i.e. head == tail)
the remove_front and remove_back functions didn't set both to NULL.

remove_front only sets the head to NULL, leaving the tail unmodified.
This causes 'double free' and 'use after free' bugs to occur.
Similarly, remove_back only sets the tail to NULL, but not the head.
Same goes for pop_front and pop_back.

We need to handle the case in which head == tail, by setting both
variables to NULL.

Vector: map, filter and reduce

Change Stack implementation

Previously, the Stack was a Linked List. This was inefficient, since
we had to malloc a node for every element, losing memory locality and
wasting bytes on the "next" pointers.

It's better to use a Vector to store the elements.
When we push to the stack, we append an element to the Vector, and
when we pop, we simply remove the last element of the vector.
These operations have a constant time complexity.

Correct use of assert

Previously, I used to assert that malloc didn't return NULL.
This is bad since assertions may be ignored (e.g. when NDEBUG
is defined). I've changed that, to make sure that if malloc returns
NULL, the error is propagated to the caller.

Also, instead of checking the parameters of the functions to
be correct I assert them.
For example:
vector_append receives a vector and an element. Previously, if one of
them was NULL, I returned NULL_PARAMETER_ERROR. Now I just assert that
they are not NULL.
